binders: For each property (i)-(v), its own existential parameter Ki > 0.
For the quantitative comparison, indices i and j range over the applicable properties and C is an absolute constant.
hypotheses: No hypothesis beyond X being a random variable is imposed for the equivalence of (i)-(iv).
The additional equivalence with (v) assumes E X = 0.
conclusions: Their positive witness parameters are quantitatively comparable up to an absolute constant factor: property i with parameter Ki implies property j with some parameter Kj <= C Ki.
If E X = 0, property (v) joins the equivalence with properties (i)-(iv), subject to the same absolute-constant quantitative comparison.
definitions_and_conventions: Property (i): there exists K1 > 0 such that P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t^2/K1^2) for every t >= 0.
Property (ii): there exists K2 > 0 such that ||X||_Lp = (E |X|^p)^(1/p) <= K2 sqrt(p) for every p >= 1.
Property (iii): there exists K3 > 0 such that E exp(lambda^2 X^2) <= exp(K3^2 lambda^2) whenever |lambda| <= 1/K3.
Property (iv): there exists K4 > 0 such that E exp(X^2/K4^2) <= 2.
Property (v): there exists K5 > 0 such that E exp(lambda X) <= exp(K5^2 lambda^2) for every lambda in R.
The phrase 'differ from each other by at most an absolute constant factor' is specified by footnote 4 as the existence of an absolute C supporting every directed conversion Kj <= C Ki.
implicit_context: The scalar expressions |X|, X^2, lambda X, inequalities, and lambda in R place the proposition in the real-valued random-variable setting, although the opening binder says only 'a random variable'.
The universal lambda in property (iii) is understood to be real from the real absolute-value condition and the surrounding discussion of real MGFs.
The word 'absolute' indicates that the comparison constant C is independent of X, the witness values, and the choice of applicable property indices.

details: The result is equivalence, not merely a one-way chain of implications.
Each listed property has its own existential positive witness parameter.
The centering hypothesis has local scope: it is required to add property (v), not to equate properties (i)-(iv).
The event uses |X| and therefore controls both tails together.
The multiplicative constant is 2, the exponent is -t^2/K1^2, and t ranges over all t >= 0.
The bound is on the Lp norm (E |X|^p)^(1/p), not directly on E |X|^p.
Growth is K2 sqrt(p), uniformly for all p >= 1.
Property (iii) uses lambda squared both in exp(lambda^2 X^2) and in exp(K3^2 lambda^2).
The allowed interval in (iii) includes its endpoints |lambda| = 1/K3.
Property (iv) is a single-point bound E exp(X^2/K4^2) <= 2 and has no universal lambda binder.
The extra premise is exactly E X = 0.
The MGF inequality is required for every real lambda, including positive and negative values.
The exponent on the right is K5^2 lambda^2, with no factor 1/2 stated.
The source does not require K1 through K5 to be equal.
For each directed implication between applicable properties, the destination witness may be chosen at most an absolute constant times the source witness.

undebatable_constraints: The equivalence of properties (i)-(iv) applies without a mean-zero assumption.
Property (v) participates in the equivalence only under E X = 0.
Every Ki is existentially quantified and strictly positive; the proposition does not posit one common K.
Property (i) must retain |X|, the factor 2, the exponent -t^2/K1^2, and the range t >= 0.
Property (ii) must retain the Lp normalization (E |X|^p)^(1/p), square-root growth in p, and the range p >= 1.
Property (iii) must retain X^2, lambda^2, the right side exp(K3^2 lambda^2), and the inclusive restriction |lambda| <= 1/K3.
Property (iv) must retain the single-point inequality E exp(X^2/K4^2) <= 2.
Property (v) must retain E exp(lambda X) <= exp(K5^2 lambda^2) for all real lambda.
Equivalence includes quantitative absolute-constant control in each implication direction, not only qualitative existence of witnesses.

ambiguities.issue: Footnote 4 literally quantifies i,j = 1,...,5 even though property (v) is introduced only under E X = 0.

ambiguities.impact: The quantitative comparison involving (v) must be read within the mean-zero branch; without that scoping, the literal footnote wording would conflict with the main statement.

contract_plain_english: For any real-valued random variable X, four ways of saying that X has sub-gaussian size are equivalent up to universal rescaling of their positive constants: a two-sided Gaussian tail bound, square-root growth of every Lp norm, a local bound for exponential moments of X squared, and a one-point exponential-square bound. If X is also centered, these are equivalent to a Gaussian bound on the ordinary moment generating function for every real lambda. The comparison is quantitative in every applicable direction: a witness constant for one property can be converted to a witness for another at a cost of at most one absolute factor.
